decision_table.name: Determine_FL_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Florida state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in FL (office, employees, property)

condition.name: has_economic_nexus
condition.comment: Meets FL economic nexus threshold ($50K or 200 transactions)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
Florida filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
Florida has physical presence nexus when corporation: - Owns or leases real property in FL - Maintains employees or agents in FL - Has an office or place of business in FL
Reference: FL Statute § 220.11 (Corporate income tax) Reference: FL Form F-1120 (Florida Corporate Income Tax Return) Reference: FL Department of Revenue Rule 12C-1.011 (Nexus)

Florida filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Florida economic nexus thresholds (lower than many states): - $50,000 or more in gross receipts from FL, OR - 200 or more separate transactions in FL
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: FL Statute § 220.14 (Apportionment of income) Reference: FL Department of Revenue TIP 22C1-02 (Economic Nexus)
No Florida nexus - no filing requirement. Any estimated payments would be refunded.

decision_table.name: Calculate_FL_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate Florida state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
Florida state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
Additions to federal taxable income: - Interest on U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to FL) - State income tax refunds included in federal income - IRC § 78 gross-up for deemed paid foreign tax credit - Addback of certain federal deductions not allowed by FL
Subtractions from federal taxable income: - Interest on municipal bonds from other states (if taxable federally) - Certain dividend income qualifying for FL exemption - Florida net operating loss deduction (separate from federal NOL) - Excess qualified production activities income deduction
Reference: FL Form F-1120 Schedule I (Adjustments to Federal Taxable Income) Reference: FL Statute § 220.13 (Computation of Florida taxable income) Reference: FL Department of Revenue Form F-1120 Instructions
No nexus - no Florida state adjustments calculated.

decision_table.name: Calculate_FL_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate Florida state corporate income tax. Applies FL 5.5% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
Florida state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to FL: × [Apportionment % - single-sales factor] 3. FL additions: + [Additions from Schedule I] 4. FL subtractions: - [Subtractions from Schedule I] 5. FL taxable income: = [Result] 6. FL tax rate: × 5.5% (flat rate) 7. FL income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. FL credits: - [Credits from Schedule II] 9. FL tax liability: = [Final tax]
Florida has a flat 5.5% corporate income tax rate on Florida taxable income.
Available FL credits include: - Enterprise zone jobs credit - Research and development credit - Community contribution tax credit - Capital investment tax credit - Renewable energy production credit - Florida Entertainment Industry Financial Incentive
Reference: FL Form F-1120 (Florida Corporate Income Tax Return) Reference: FL Statute § 220.11 (Tax rate: 5.5%) Reference: FL Statute § 220.13 (Florida taxable income computation) Reference: FL Statute § 220.14 (Single-sales factor apportionment) Reference: FL Statute § 220.181-.197 (Tax credits)
No Florida nexus - no tax liability. Any estimated payments are refunded.

No Florida taxable income - no tax liability.
Florida allows net operating loss (NOL) carryforwards: - NOLs may be carried forward up to 20 years - NOL carryback not allowed under FL law - FL NOL calculated separately from federal NOL
Reference: FL Statute § 220.13(1)(b) (NOL deduction)
